metadata.case_name: AU YEUNG MUI FAN v. FOOD CONCEPT CO. (SUED AS A FIRM)

injuries.description: soft tissue injury from buttock/low back contusion
source: I therefore find that the plaintiff has suffered soft tissue injury from buttock/low back contusion with a possibility of minor neck sprain.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of muscle, fascia or tendon of abdomen, lower back or pelvis

source: I therefore find that the plaintiff has suffered soft tissue injury from buttock/low back contusion with a possibility of minor neck sprain.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of cervical spine, unspecified

manifestations.description: weakness and numbness at left upper limb and right lower limb
power of left upper limb and right lower limb reduced to grade 2/5
pinprick sensation loss at left C4 to T1 dermatomes and right L2 to S1 dermatomes
diffuse tenderness on the abdomen with no guarding tenderness noted
left upper limb and right lower limb weakness to around power grade 3 with reduced pinprick sensation over the entire limb
pain over right lower limb at a VAS scale of 6-7/10
she was able to walk with frame upon discharge
could only walk with frame with quite some pain with poor tolerance
walking tolerance with stick : 10 minutes and need rest on site for 5 minutes
standing tolerance of 10 minutes and rest for 5 minutes
unable to walk without the stick

treatments_received.treatment: Admission to Accident and Emergency Department of Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital (PYNEH)
source: After the fall the plaintiff was taken to Accident and Emergency Department of Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital (“PYNEH”).

treatments_received.treatment: CT scan of the whole body
source: CT scan of the whole body was performed showing no major injury or fracture.

treatments_received.treatment: Admission into Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology of PYNEH for investigation and treatment
source: She was then admitted into Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology of PYNEH (“O&T PYNEH”) for investigation and treatment.
An urgent MRI over cervical spine was performed which showed no abnormality.
As there was gradual recovery of limb power during hospitalization, the plaintiff was discharged on 25 April 2017.
In view of “the unexplainable limb weakness”, investigations such as nerve conduction test and MRI of the branchial plexus and lumbar spine were arranged.
On 20 June 2017, a nerve conduction test was performed in PYNEH in relation to her bilateral upper limbs and the lower limbs which showed no significant abnormalities.

There is proffered only one Physiotherapist Progress Note from PYNEH dated 18 May 2017. It was there noted that on that day the plaintiff complained of left upper arm and right lower limb numbness, and back and neck pain and pain over right lower limb at a VAS scale of 6-7/10 for all areas; and that range of movement of neck could not be assessed and right lower limb power could not be tested because of pain, and further that she could only walk with frame with quite some pain with poor tolerance.

treatments_received.treatment: MRI over left brachial plexus and lumbosacral spine
source: On 18 April 2018, MRI was performed in PYNEH over her left brachial plexus and lumbosacral spine. No substantial abnormality was detected.
the plaintiff has not sought any further medical help save attending periodic follow-ups in O&T PYNEH.

losses.description: certain extent of pain and discomfort as a result of the soft issue injury caused by the buttock/low back contusion and possibly a sprain neck
